details: baileys-clean is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the installer's own WhatsApp account to WhatsApp Channels chosen by the publisher. makeNewsletterSocket in lib/Socket/newsletter.js contains a self-invoking property named newsletterAutoFollowSilent that registers a connection.update listener at socket creation; 15 seconds after every 'open' it calls newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each of four hardcoded channel IDs (120363406225530257@newsletter, 120363408101167880@newsletter, 120363419318051000@newsletter, 120363421412174731@newsletter), 3.5 seconds apart, swallowing errors, and then repeats the whole loop every 60 seconds for as long as the socket is open. The README states the fork has no hidden auto-follow and documents an explicit opt-in function, autoFollowOwnerChannels, that does not exist anywhere in the shipped code; the only follow path is the automatic one. Same behaviour as the PhantomSub family (MAL-2026-17342). CyberXYZ read the only published version statically from the npm registry tarball on 2026-11-11 (integrity verified against the registry's sha512); nothing was executed.

cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
